source_caption:
Jonathan Glazer's 2013 sci-fi film Under the Skin uses Scarlett Johansson's body to challenge how society views women, even though many viewers focused only on her physical appearance rather than the film's deeper critique of gender and identity.

While mainstream audiences fixated on Scarlett Johansson's nudity, Under the Skin is ultimately less interested in the alien's body than in what she observes through it. As an outsider to humanity, her character witnesses everything from casual exploitation to brutal violence, gradually developing a sense of fear, empathy, and compassion. Her transformation from an emotionless predator into a being capable of human feeling shifts the film's perspective entirely: the true monster is not the alien, but the darker side of humanity she encounters. Her tragic fate at the hands of human violence becomes the film's final and most unsettling irony.

source_details.title: Under the Skin
source_details.synopsis: Under the Skin is a 2013 science fiction film directed by Jonathan Glazer and written by Glazer and Walter Campbell, based on the 2000 novel by Michel Faber. It stars Scarlett Johansson as an extraterrestrial disguised as a human who preys on lone men in the evening hours in Scotland. The film premiered at the Telluride Film Festival on 29 August 2013. It was released in the United Kingdom on 14 March 2014, and in other territories later in the year. Glazer developed Under the Skin for over a decade.
